Why can't astronauts on the Moon talk to each other directly, without radios?
questions.answer: There is no air on the Moon. Sound needs a medium to travel, so it cannot pass through the empty space between them.

questions.q: Which part of the ear vibrates when sound reaches it? Why should we never put sharp objects into our ears?
questions.answer: The eardrum. A sharp object can damage the eardrum, which can affect hearing.

questions.q: What is the difference between music and noise?
questions.answer: Sounds that are pleasant to hear are called music. Unpleasant sounds are called noise. Even music becomes noise when it is too loud.

questions.q: Give two sources of noise pollution and two of its harmful effects.
questions.answer: Sources (any two): vehicle horns, loudspeakers, firecrackers, factory machines, loud TV or music. Effects (any two): lack of sleep, high blood pressure, anxiety, hearing loss.

questions.q: Which part vibrates to produce sound in (a) a sitar, (b) a flute, (c) a dholak?
questions.answer: (a) Sitar: the stretched strings. (b) Flute: the air column inside the tube. (c) Dholak: the stretched membrane (skin).

subparts.q: How is the human voice produced?
subparts.answer: The voice box (larynx) at the upper end of the windpipe has two vocal cords with a narrow slit between them. When air from the lungs is forced through the slit, the vocal cords vibrate and produce sound.

subparts.q: Why are men's voices usually deeper than women's?
subparts.answer: Men's vocal cords are longer (about 20 mm, compared with about 15 mm in women), so they vibrate at a lower frequency, giving a lower pitch.

subparts.q: Suggest two ways to reduce noise near a school.
subparts.answer: (Any two) Plant trees along the roads around the school; put up 'No horn' signs and enforce them; keep loud vehicles and factories away; use sound-absorbing materials in classrooms.
